 Medium
 Large
 Print The Full Moon in Taurus encourages us to reflect on what we cling to for security. With Venus in retrograde in Scorpio, it's time to reevaluate past decisions and their significance today. While the process of letting go might feel daunting, it paves the way for personal growth and fresh opportunities. By implementing minor adjustments, we can learn to navigate these changes gracefully, balancing comfort with self-improvement. Today's spiritual lesson is that comfort and growth are not always on the same side. What feels safe can slowly become a small room. Spiritual Quote of the Day "Some things are kept out of habit, and the habit is the only thing holding them." The Full Moon in Taurus Brings Things to Light 
 A Full Moon marks the peak of a lunar cycle. What the New Moon set in motion becomes visible, and so does whatever has been left unfinished. This one falls in Taurus, an earth sign tied to comfort, possessions and steady routine. Attention turns to what has been held onto, and why. Taurus Holds On Well 
 Taurus is loyal and patient. It does not drop things lightly. That strength matters when something is worth keeping. But the same trait can keep an outdated arrangement going long after it's no longer useful. A subscription nobody opens. A friendship that continues only by reflex. A savings plan not reviewed in years. Venus Retrograde Adds Review 
 Taurus is ruled by Venus, which is retrograde in Scorpio. Venus governs value, so the question becomes what is still worth its place. Retrograde motion favours revisiting old choices before making new ones. Ask what was accepted once and never checked again. Why Letting Go Feels Risky 
 Familiar things promise predictability. Removing one leaves a gap, and the gap feels unsafe, even when what filled it did little. That is why a person may stay in a stale situation for years. But a gap can also be room. A cleared shelf makes room for something better. Release in Small Steps 
 You don't have to throw everything out at once. Pick one item, one commitment or one habit. Cancel the unused service. Decline the recurring obligation that no one enjoys. Tidy one drawer and note what it feels like. A small release shows whether you need a larger one. It builds confidence in your ability to cope with less. What October 26 Asks of You 
 Choose one thing you keep only because it feels safe. Ask what it gives you now, and what it costs. If the cost is higher, set a date to let it go. The zodiac now favours the person who keeps what serves them and releases what no longer does.
